issues.legal_issue: An acquisition for planned development of a large area is not invalid merely because the particular use of each parcel has not been specified in the development plans when the acquisition is initiated.
material_facts: The acquisition covered a large area comprising numerous plots for the stated public purpose of planned development.
The land in question had not been specifically allocated to a particular use in the relevant development plans, and some of it lay within a cantonment area.
The development plans and related planning activities were to be implemented after the land became available through acquisition.
issues.conclusion: The acquisition notification was not invalid because it did not particularise the intended use of the specific land; the specified purpose of planned development was a public purpose.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 3(f) and 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, planned development is a public purpose. For an acquisition of a large area comprising plots belonging to different owners, identifying the particular use of every parcel is not a condition precedent to initiating acquisition. The planning details may be worked out after acquisition. The Court relied on Aflatoon v. Lt. Governor, Smt. Ratni Devi v. Chief Commissioner, Pt. Lila Ram v. Union of India, Om Prakash v. Union of India, Ram Chand v. Union of India, State of Tamil Nadu v. L. Krishanan, and Jai Narain v. Union of India; it also noted that Section 12(3)(ii) of the Delhi Development Act addresses development in cantonment areas.

rule.if: appeal_challenges_land_acquisition and acquisition_for_planned_development and acquisition_covers_large_area_with_multiple_plots and public_purpose_is_specified and individual_parcel_use_is_not_specified

predicates.appeal_challenges_land_acquisition: An appeal challenges the validity of a land acquisition.
predicates.acquisition_for_planned_development: The acquiring authority seeks land for planned development.
predicates.acquisition_covers_large_area_with_multi: The acquisition covers a large area comprising multiple plots.
predicates.public_purpose_is_specified: The acquisition notice identifies a public purpose for which the land is sought.
predicates.individual_parcel_use_is_not_specified: The intended specific use of each individual parcel has not been identified when acquisition is initiated.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges an acquisition for planned development covering multiple plots and the public purpose is stated, the absence of a specified use for each parcel does not make such specification necessary before acquisition.

issues.legal_issue: The requirement to publish the substance of an acquisition notification in the locality is satisfied when the official record supports local publication and the evidence does not rebut the presumption that official acts were regularly performed.
material_facts: Publication of the acquisition notification in the Gazette was undisputed.

The official record included endorsements that a copy had been received and would be affixed at a conspicuous place, and that copies had been affixed at public offices and at the site through the village headman.
The record and the High Court's examination of it supported the finding that the substance of the notification was affixed in the locality.
The Supreme Court examined the record and found the locality publication had occurred; it did not require proof beyond reasonable doubt.
issues.conclusion: The substance of the notification was duly published in the locality, so the locality-publication requirement was complied with.
issues.legal_principle: Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 requires publication of the notification in the Gazette and publication of its substance in the locality; omission of either requirement renders the notification void. Section 114(e) of the Evidence Act permits a presumption that official acts have been regularly performed unless the presumption is displaced by evidence. The Court relied on Khub Chand v. State of Rajasthan for the mandatory nature of the publication requirements.

predicates.appeal_challenges_land_acquisition: An appeal challenges the validity of a land acquisition.
predicates.official_records_support_local_publicati: Official records indicate that the substance of the acquisition notice was affixed in the locality.
predicates.contrary_evidence_does_not_displace_regu: The evidence offered against the official records does not overcome the presumption that the recorded official acts were regularly performed.

issues.definition: In an appeal challenging an acquisition, locality publication is treated as satisfied when official records support it and contrary evidence does not displace the presumption of regular official performance.
